title: Prefill vs decode pipeline optimizations: chunked prefill, speculative prefill, and stage overlap
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: reduce end-to-end latency and improve throughput for mixed prefill+decode request patterns (chat-style workloads). This PR introduces three orthogonal optimizations to the serving runtime pipeline: 1) chunked prefill: break large prefill KV loads into smaller chunks to allow earlier decode start and reduce blocking on long prefill fills; 2) speculative prefill: proactively prefetch likely KV segments for follow-on requests based on prefix heuristics and cached sequence fingerprints; 3) stage overlap: restructure the pipeline to allow overlap between the prefill (KV loading/compilation) stage and the decode stage where safe, via a lightweight readiness protocol that gates attention/kvcache access. Changes are conservative by default and gated by feature flags and a new policy config per model. Backward compatibility: all changes are opt-in and fall back to the existing pipeline when disabled. This description covers motivation, design, tests, and benchmark results. Design: - Chunked prefill: introduce a chunker that splits a prefill into N-token windows (configurable per-model and per-request). Each chunk issues KV-load work units that can be scheduled independently. When the first chunk is loaded the runtime can start compiling kernels and start decoding if the decode path does not require later chunks for correctness (heuristic below). - Speculative prefill: add a speculative prefetcher that uses recent prefix fingerprints plus a lightweight n-gram probability model to decide the next-most-likely KV shards to warm. Speculation is rate-limited and only used when the cluster is underutilized; it also honors privacy and KMS constraints (no speculation for encrypted private models). - Stage overlap / decode overlap windows: add a coordinated protocol where decode workers can begin consuming KV caches that are marked as "ready_for_read" for the portion they need. Partial reads are supported; if a decode tries to access a not-yet-loaded segment, it falls back to a short blocking wait or switches to a faster but slightly higher-cost memory-based fallback path. Safety: correctness preserved by verifying KV-shard checksums and version stamps before using partially-loaded caches. Implementation highlights: - runtime/scheduler: new scheduling unit 'prefill_chunk' with priority and backpressure rules. - runtime/kvcache: chunked shard API, checksum/version metadata, speculative warming interface. - runtime/pipeline: readiness flag propagation, decode gating, and fallback path. - configs: model-level flags, per-route heuristics, and admin feature gates. Tests: unit tests for chunker, speculative prefetcher, readiness protocol; integration tests in perf-canary harness; stress tests for concurrent mixed prefill+decode traffic. Benchmarks: - Microbench (single-host, 8xA100, 1k-token prefill followed by streaming decode): baseline median latency 420ms -> chunked prefill + overlap 310ms (26% median reduction), speculative prefill + overlap 295ms (30% median reduction). - Throughput (75th percentile latency SLO 500ms): throughput increased ~18% at target SLO on mixed workloads. - Cost note: speculative prefetch adds ~2-4% extra token-equivalent work under typical settings; tuned heuristics keep this low. Rollout plan: feature gated per-customer; default off for enterprise private deployments until API flag enabled. Opt-in flag names: runtime.prefill.chunked, runtime.prefill.speculative, runtime.pipeline.overlap. Related work: ENG-1023 (batching improvements), ENG-1105 (kvcache refactor). See inline files changed for details.

review_conversation: Liam Chen: Nice work. A couple of questions: how does this interact with existing continuous batching? Could prefill chunks interfere with batching heuristics?

Ava Martinez: We added a scheduler hook so chunked prefill units are coalesced when the batcher is in coalescing window; chunk size heuristics prefer chunk boundaries aligned to batch-friendly sizes to avoid fragmentation.
Priya Nair: Need to be careful about memory growth with speculative warming. How is eviction handled?
Ava Martinez: Speculative warms are marked with low TTL and a speculative flag; eviction policy prioritizes non-speculative shards. We added metrics to monitor warmed shard ratio and memory overhead.
Omar Haddad: CI failed on one run (flake). Can you re-run and add a test to prevent regression?
Ava Martinez: Re-ran CI and added a targeted integration test for concurrent prefill chunk interleaving (tests/integration/test_pipeline_overlap.py).
Liam Chen: Approve after test added and one doc nit is fixed.
release_notes: Performance: reduce prefill+decode median latency by ~26-30% for long-prefill chat workloads via chunked prefill, speculative warming, and decode-prefill stage overlap. Admins: feature flags runtime.prefill.chunked, runtime.prefill.speculative, runtime.pipeline.overlap; default off for private deployments. Impact: ~18% higher throughput at 75th percentile SLO; speculative prefetch increases warm work by ~2-4% typical.
